This page is for **contributors** extending the Studyflow language with new element types or attributes. If you are a researcher or pipeline author using the modeler, see the [Elements](../reference/elements.qmd) reference instead.

Studyflow uses direct moddle YAML as the authoring format for schema definitions. The schemas live in `src/assets/schemas/` and ship with the modeler. Five are **core** (`core: true` -- always loaded, cannot be disabled from the settings); the rest are domain extensions you can switch on:

| File | Prefix | What it declares |
|---|---|---|
| `studyflow.moddle.yaml` | `studyflow` | The core language: `Study`, `StartEvent`, `EndEvent`, `SequenceFlow`, the `BaseElement`/`Scheduling`/`Classification` traits, and the data-infrastructure types (`Schema`, `Dataset`, `DataCatalog`, `Table`, `Timeseries`, `EventMarker`). It also declares the inspector's tabs for every schema. **core** |
| `exec.moddle.yaml` | `exec` | The executable layer: `implementation` and its `additionalArguments`, the run `seed`, the association `binding`, the timer/condition/loop expressions, artifact `uri` (its `format` belongs to the data types), and `Parameters`. **core** |
| `functional.moddle.yaml` | `functional` | `Transform`, `Map`, `Reduce`, `Filter` -- the generic verbs domain layers root their presets on. **core** |
| `cognitive.moddle.yaml` | `cognitive` | `CognitiveTask`, `Rest`, `Questionnaire`, `Instruction`, `BehaverseTask`, `RandomGateway`, `EligibilityGateway`, `Actor`. Split out of the core so adopters can swap the cognitive layer. **core** |
| `agentic.moddle.yaml` | `agentic` | LLM and agent workflows: `Agent`, `Router`, `LLMCall`, `Tool`, `HumanApproval`, `Prompt`, `Memory`. |
| `ml.moddle.yaml` | `ml` | scikit-learn pipeline presets. Templates only -- it declares no types. |
| `datatrove.moddle.yaml` | `datatrove` | The datatrove library's `Reader`/`Writer` IO blocks. |
| `omniprocess.moddle.yaml` | `omniprocess` | Neuroimaging preprocessing presets (fMRIPrep, EEGPrep). Templates only. |
| `openbci.moddle.yaml` | `openbci` | `OpenBCISession` and `OpenBCIRecording` for biosignal acquisition. |

Note the core schema's `name` and `prefix` differ: it is named `Core` but prefixed `studyflow`, because the prefix appears in every saved file and the URI is the stable identifier old files are matched by.

## Core structure

Studyflow moddle YAML files follow this top-level layout:

```yaml
name: Core
prefix: studyflow
description: Core BPMN extension for modeling research processes.
uri: http://behaverse.org/schemas/studyflow/v1   # version segment = studyflow format version
legacyUris:                                      # optional: namespaces older releases wrote
  - http://behaverse.org/schemas/studyflow       # still read, rewritten to `uri` on load
icon: iconify tabler--hexagon-letter-s   # optional, shown in the modeler
core: true          # optional: always loaded, cannot be disabled
order: 10           # registry position (load precedence + settings order)
version: 26.0716
xml:
  tagAlias: lowerCase
categories: []      # inspector tabs; only the core schema declares these
associations: []
enumerations: []
types: []
templates: []
```

The `description` is shown in the schema palette -- keep it to a sentence or two, since it renders in a tooltip. The optional `icon` (URL or `iconify <name>`) appears next to the schema name.

## Inspector tabs (`categories`)

A property names the tab it appears under in `meta.categories`. The tabs themselves are declared **once, in the core schema**, and every other schema files into them:

`General` · `Documentation` · `Gantt` · `Data` · `Execution` · `Run record`

A tab has to earn its name: these are the questions a modeller asks of *any* element, which is why they recur across schemas. A tab holding a single type's own fields would only repeat what the panel header already says the element is, so those fields go to `General` -- an OpenBCI recording has no "OpenBCI" tab and an LLM call has no "Model call" tab. Naming a category no schema declares still works, but it sorts after every declared one, so prefer the six above.

`Execution` and `Run record` are special. `Execution` is `synthetic: true`: a dedicated section component draws it over nested BPMN state (properties, data associations, loop characteristics), so it appears even with no attributes filed under it. `Run record` is where engine-written fields go (`meta.readonly: true`), kept last so run records sit apart from what people author.

## Enumerations

`enumerations` define reusable closed value lists referenced from properties via `type:`.

```yaml
enumerations:
  - name: CompletionCodeTypeEnum
    isAbstract: true
    description: How the completion code is generated when the study ends.
    literalValues:
      - name: None
        value: none
        description: No completion code is issued.
      - name: Static
        value: static
      - name: Dynamic
        value: dynamic
```

Properties typed with an enum can opt into free-text entry alongside the enum values by setting `meta.editable: true`.

## Types and properties

Each moddle type defines a domain element plus the properties shown in the inspector. Two relationships compose types:

- **`extends`** -- pure mixin onto an existing BPMN class. Use it when you only want to *add* attributes to a BPMN base (e.g. extend `bpmn:StartEvent` with `consentFormUri`) without creating a new visual element. A type with `extends` and `isAbstract: true` is a **trait**: it is never placed on the canvas, it only contributes attributes to whatever it names.
- **`superClass`** -- class inheritance. Use it when defining a new concrete element. List the BPMN base first (e.g. `bpmn:Task`, `bpmn:ExclusiveGateway`, `bpmn:DataStoreReference`) and add `bpmn:BaseElement` so the inspector picks up the standard metadata fields.

Pair `superClass` with `meta.bpmnType` so the modeler knows which BPMN shape to render.

```yaml
types:
  - name: StartEvent
    extends:
      - bpmn:StartEvent
    isAbstract: true
    properties:
      - name: consentFormUri
        description: Link to the consent form. Untick to skip the consent step.
        isAttr: true
        type: String
        meta:
          optional: true
          categories:
            - General

  - name: RandomGateway
    description: Assigns participants to an outgoing branch at random.
    superClass:
      - bpmn:ExclusiveGateway
      - bpmn:BaseElement
    meta:
      icon: iconify streamline-flex--dice-5
      bpmnType: bpmn:ExclusiveGateway
    properties:
      - name: algorithm
        isAttr: true
        type: studyflow:AssignmentAlgorithmEnum
        default: probabilistic
        meta:
          categories:
            - General
```

### Redefining a BPMN attribute

bpmn-moddle already carries every BPMN attribute, and the inspector shows **none** of them: a field renders only when a schema declares it. `redefines` is how a native attribute becomes editable -- and where this project writes down what it means:

```yaml
- name: Implementation
  extends:
    - bpmn:ServiceTask
  isAbstract: true
  properties:
    - name: bpmn:implementation
      description: Software this step runs, as `<scheme>://<ref>[@<version>]`.
      isAttr: true
      type: String
      redefines: bpmn:ServiceTask#implementation
```

Delete that trait and the field disappears from the panel while the attribute stays in the file. So a schema's `redefines` list is not a copy of the BPMN metamodel -- it is this layer's list of which BPMN attributes a studyflow author edits.

### Property modifiers

Property entries carry moddle behavior directly:

- `isAttr: true` -- serialized as an XML attribute in the BPMN XML form (most scalar properties). The YAML `.studyflow` format maps every property to a plain key regardless of this flag.
- `isBody: true` -- serialized as the element's text body in the BPMN XML form. Used for free-form content like YAML `configurations`.
- `isMany: true` -- repeated property (rendered as a list in the inspector).
- `default` -- initial value.
- `redefines` -- override the type, default, or visibility of an inherited property (see above).
- `replaces` -- replace an inherited property entirely.
- `xml.serialize: property` / `xsi:type` -- how a complex-typed property is written. Needed when redefining BPMN's own expression elements, which are named after the property rather than the type.

Studyflow-specific modeler behavior lives under `meta` on the property:

- `meta.categories: [Data]` -- the tab the property lives under (see above).
- `meta.order: 1` -- position within its tab; unordered properties sort after ordered ones.
- `meta.pinned: true` -- always visible, even when the value is empty.
- `meta.optional: true` -- the inspector shows a checkbox to opt the property in.
- `meta.editable: true` -- enum properties also accept free-text entries.
- `meta.editor: code` -- which input component edits it (`code`, `markdown`, `csvw-table`). A value *type* may name one for all its properties instead, which is how every `studyflow:YAMLString` gets the code editor.
- `meta.readonly: true` -- display-only; written by the runner, not by hand.
- `meta.legacyNames: [category]` -- earlier spellings still read from old files and rewritten on save.
- `meta.condition.language: json` + `meta.condition.body: { otherField: value }` -- visibility predicate; the property only appears when other fields match. A value of `$set` matches whenever the other field has any value.

`meta` on the *type* carries `icon`, `bpmnType`, `editor`, and `roles` -- a list of capability tags (`data-element`, `signal`, `instrument`, …) that lets the app find types by what they are rather than by name. Most roles are inferred from the type graph; declare one only when it adds something inference cannot see.

## Function calls (`implementation` / `arguments`)

Any activity can declare the software that implements it. BPMN's own `implementation` attribute (redefined once by the `exec` schema) carries the reference, and the core `studyflow:Arguments` trait (which mixes onto every `bpmn:Activity`) carries the arguments:

- `implementation` -- a scheme-prefixed reference, `<scheme>://<ref>[@<version-or-digest>]`. Recognized schemes are `python://` (an importable callable, e.g. `python://sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline.fit`), `docker://` (an image, e.g. `docker://ghcr.io/lab/img@sha256:...`), `https://` (a script URL), and `file://` (a local script). Other schemes are allowed but flagged as unresolved -- a cognitive task imported from jsPsych names its plugin as `jspsych://...`. The ref/version split happens at the last `@`, so docker digests parse correctly.
- `additionalArguments` -- a `studyflow:YAMLString` holding the literal arguments (the role GitHub Actions' `with:` block plays), *additional* by name and by contract: the associations fill the signature first -- each data input association binds its element to the slot its `binding` names -- and this supplies what is left over. Anything the step *reads* is a data association, not an entry here; a name bound by both is an error rather than a precedence question. The reserved `args` key lists positional arguments, and a nested mapping carrying its own `implementation` is a call resolved before the outer one.

A data association carries one `exec:binding` — `slot = selection`, each half optional. The slot names *which* callable parameter the value fills (blank binds by the element's own name; `self` binds an unbound method's receiver, `*` appends positionally, the only way into `train_test_split(*arrays)`); the selection narrows *what* value arrives, as member access and indexing (`folds['train']`). On an output association the drawn target is the slot, so the binding is a selection over `result` (`result[0]`) — which is how one call fills several properties. Selections coordinate, they never compute: anything that calculates is a step with its own `implementation`. Saved XML never carries the attribute — it lowers to BPMN's native `ioSpecification` + `transformation` spelling and folds back on open.

```yaml
Fit:
  implementation: python://sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline.fit
  dataInputAssociations:
    Association_Estimator:
      binding: self             # the receiver: bound first, positionally
      sourceRef: [Estimator]
    Association_Features:
      binding: X
      sourceRef: [X_Train]
  additionalArguments:
    sample_weight: null         # what the associations did not supply
```

Both halves in one attribute, when the step wants a slice of what the element
holds rather than all of it:

```yaml
Score:
  implementation: python://sklearn.metrics.accuracy_score
  dataInputAssociations:
    Association_Truth:
      binding: y_true = folds['test']   # which slot, and what arrives there
      sourceRef: [Folds]
```

In the BPMN XML form, `implementation` is an attribute on the activity and `additionalArguments` is an `<exec:additionalArguments>` child element holding the YAML as its text; both round-trip losslessly through the `.studyflow` YAML form, where `arguments` inlines as a nested mapping. An activity carrying an `implementation` value shows a function marker on the canvas.

The browser runner parses and validates the call but does not execute it. The Python runner in `src/runner/python/` does: it resolves the reference, materializes the associated inputs, calls it, and binds the return value, writing an as-run record per run. `src/assets/examples/sklearn_pipeline.png` is the worked example it is checked against -- see `src/runner/python/README.md`.

## Templates

Schemas may define top-level `templates` entries -- preset elements that appear in the palette flyouts, the command palette, and the template gallery. Each entry uses `object.type` to name the schema type (or BPMN type) to instantiate, plus any default property values to apply.

This is the mechanism behind a recurring design rule: **parameterize, don't proliferate.** A verb that is just a generic step bound to a function (extract, tokenize, fit, fMRIPrep…) ships as a template, not as a new element type. `ml` and `omniprocess` declare no types at all for this reason.

```yaml
templates:
  - description: Preprocess fMRI data for a single subject (fMRIPrep in a container).
    object:
      type: functional:Map
      bpmn:name: fMRIPrep
      bpmn:documentation: Runs fMRIPrep over one subject's BIDS directory.
      icon: iconify icon-park--brain
      keywords:              # matched by the command palette's search
        - fmriprep
        - preprocessing
      implementation: docker://nipreps/fmriprep@sha256:...
      arguments: |
        output_spaces: MNI152NLin2009cAsym
```

`keywords` is how a template is found by typing rather than by browsing; give each one the words a user would actually reach for.

### Template mixins

`object.mixins` lets a template compose additional defaults from other types. This is useful when the preset should behave like a specialized BPMN shape without changing the underlying schema class.

```yaml
templates:
  - description: Preprocess EEG data for a single subject.
    object:
      type: functional:Map
      bpmn:name: Preprocess EEG
      mixins:
        - bpmn:SubProcess
```

Use `mixins` for template-time composition, not for reusable schema inheritance -- that belongs on `types[].superClass`.

### Nested flow elements

A template that resolves to `bpmn:SubProcess` may declare `object.flowElements` to create internal nodes and connections along with the root sub-process. The `exec` schema's "Repeat until" template does this to stamp out a whole loop idiom -- a gateway, a conditioned back-edge, and an exit:

```yaml
templates:
  - description: Retry-until-good loop, drawn.
    object:
      bpmn:name: Repeat until
      type: bpmn:SubProcess
      flowElements:
        - id: loop_start
          type: bpmn:StartEvent
          x: 140
          y: 150
        - id: loop_work
          type: bpmn:Task
          bpmn:name: Do the work
          x: 220
          y: 130
        - type: bpmn:SequenceFlow
          sourceRef: loop_start
          targetRef: loop_work
```

A template may also declare `object.attributes` for promoted attributes specific to that preset:

```yaml
templates:
  - description: Preprocess EEG data for a single subject.
    object:
      type: functional:Map
      bpmn:name: EEGPrep
      attributes:
        param1:
          range: string
          description: Template-specific promoted attribute.
          ifabsent: default_value
```

These are not added back onto the schema class. The modeler generates a template-scoped derived moddle type for that object, so the extra attributes persist in the saved diagram (in both serializations) without changing other templates or the base class. Undeclared scalar properties on the object are inferred onto the same derived type.

## Cross-schema references

Use the schema prefix to reference types from another schema, e.g. `studyflow:YAMLString`, `studyflow:AssignmentAlgorithmEnum`, `studyflow:Dataset`. The functional schema, for example, refers to `functional:Transform#operationType` when pinning a verb's `operationType` on subtypes like `Map`, and `openbci:OpenBCIRecording` extends `studyflow:Dataset`.

## Common mistakes

- **Prefix mismatch**: the core schema is prefixed `studyflow`, not `core` -- its `name` is Core but nothing references it by that. Its unversioned URI is legacy and lives in `legacyUris`.
- **Missing `type`**: moddle properties without a type fall back to string-like behavior and may produce unintended interfaces.
- **Mixing up `extends` and `superClass`**: use `extends` to mix attributes onto an existing BPMN base; use `superClass` to define a new concrete type.
- **Expecting a native BPMN attribute to appear**: it will not until a schema `redefines` it.
- **Inventing a tab**: a category no schema declares sorts after every declared one. File the property under one of the six instead.
- **Incorrect BPMN mapping**: omit or misconfigure `meta.bpmnType` and the element may no longer map to the intended BPMN shape.
- **Invalid condition shape**: malformed `condition.body` JSON disables conditional visibility.
- **Incorrect `redefines` owner**: invalid targets are dropped.
- **A long `description`**: it renders in a tooltip, so keep it to one or two sentences. Rationale belongs in these docs or in a YAML comment.

## Naming conventions

Property names follow camelCase (`consentFormUri`, `completionCodeType`), except where a value mirrors an external tool's CLI one-to-one -- e.g. the fMRIPrep template's `output_spaces` argument matches the corresponding flag verbatim, so configurations can be copy-pasted.
